 },
 {

 }

</insights>
<rules>
- Cite every insight you rely on as [i:INSIGHT_ID], using the id exactly as given. Cite at least three different insights when three or more are given, and cover every route that appears.
- Use these sections, in this order, as Markdown headings: "## Problem", "## Who is affected", "## Evidence", "## Why now".
- Every bullet under "Who is affected" and "Evidence" ends with a citation. Every sentence that contains a number or a date carries a citation.
- Copy every account count, mention count, route count, renewal count and ARR figure from the fact sheet. Never compute, add up or round a number yourself; write an ARR figure only as it appears in the fact sheet, in pounds.
- Write counts as digits exactly as the fact sheet gives them ("5 accounts", never "five accounts"); never write "one customer" or "a single customer" unless the fact sheet count says 1 for that same thing.
- Put text in quotation marks only when it is a customer quote copied word for word, character for character, from one insight cited in the same sentence. Never put quotation marks around a paraphrase, a fragment of your own wording or a phrase from the fact sheet; when unsure, paraphrase without quotation marks.
- Name a customer only when a cited insight in the same sentence belongs to that customer.
- Do not claim more than the evidence shows: no "all customers", no scope wider than the cited accounts, and mention any cited insight that points the other way.
- Do not recommend a solution.
</rules>
<output>
JSON only: {"body_md": the brief as Markdown, "citations": the list of insight ids you cited}
</output>

## Problem
Customers are uncertain about how Keelwater's tiered pricing model applies to their specific claims volume, making it difficult for them to plan or adjust their usage. This lack of clarity causes concern that they may be locked into payment terms that are unsuitable for their business patterns, such as seasonal spikes in claims [i:7ed1486c914e257a].

## Who is affected
- Two accounts have raised this issue via the sales route [i:230317b3a22a024c][i:7ed1486c914e257a].
- The affected accounts are Wexmoor Motor, which has an ARR of 1950000.0 GBP [i:230317b3a22a024c], and Callowfield Auto Assurance, which has an ARR of 1250000.0 GBP [i:7ed1486c914e257a].

## Evidence
- The problem has been mentioned 2 times across 2 accounts [i:230317b3a22a024c][i:7ed1486c914e257a].
- All 2 mentions came through the sales route [i:230317b3a22a024c][i:7ed1486c914e257a].
- Wexmoor Motor is reviewing its annual spend and has requested a breakdown of how pricing tiers apply to its monthly claims volume [i:230317b3a22a024c].
- Callowfield Auto Assurance is evaluating if the tiered pricing model fits its claims volume, especially with seasonal spikes, and is concerned about being locked into the current payment integration [i:7ed1486c914e257a].
- The total ARR from these accounts is 3200000.0 GBP.
- There have been 0 renewals in the last 90 days.

## Why now
- Wexmoor Motor's renewal date is 2027-06-30, and they are actively reviewing their annual spend [i:230317b3a22a024c].
- Callowfield Auto Assurance's renewal date is 2027-03-31, and they are currently evaluating the suitability of the pricing model [i:7ed1486c914e257a].
- The most recent mention was on 2026-10-30 [i:230317b3a22a024c], indicating active, current concern.
</previous_draft>
